title: A good start, but needs work
body: This application contains good menus with a wide range of cuisines, but it is not as usable as it might be. The workflow starts by providing a selection of meals for a period of time, matching your dietary profile. From there, you can edit the menu, but the fact that you can do this is not obvious from the UI. Once you generate a shopping list, there’s no way to lock the list of menu items to the shopping list, so it’s easy to accidentally modify that menu. If you already use an alternate shopping list, it’s very difficult to transfer the list from this application to another one. Marking a meal “cooked“ produces no visual change in the list of menu items. Once you start cooking, the app really falls apart. I find myself constantly, switching back-and-forth between the ingredients view and the instructions, and the instruction flow does not actually match the kitchen flow very well. Three examples: 1. I have a selected recipe that takes 2 1/2 hours to make because of a 2 hour required marination time, but that is not reflected in the prep time. 2. I just finished executing a recipe that requires adding ingredients to boiling pasta, but that step is four or five steps down in the recipe, after the pasta is complete. 3. None of the recipes include the amount of herbs and spices; you have to pluck that off the ingredients list. The developers would do well to examine an application like MealLime, or a cookbook like Joy of Cooking, to see how this can be alleviated.

If 1 of 4 is vegetarian have a meal plan with a meat entree, a vegetarian entree that could double as a side, a 2nd vegetable side and a whatever else is in the plan for that meal. title: Accurate pricing to store price!!
body: This app has saved so much time and took away the time it takes me to sit down and think of meals for the week! They give you a grocery list to shop for the items you need for your meals at your preferred store. Also the pricing is on point to the price at my store. It was only off by $0.25 which is totally fine with me, especially with one of my meals being steak for the week! I gave it a $150 budget but the meal plan for the week was only $108. And that meal plan included things like a steak and peppercorn sauce, Chicken Caesar wrap, Spaghetti Bolognese, BBQ loaded chicken wrap, homemade burgers, and a chili cheese beef pasta! My plan I for 3 people! So this is awesome!

title: Extremely helpful!!!
body: This app is basically Home Chef or Hello Fresh without food being delivered to your house. This app is great for families, single living or if your just living with your partner and have no clue what to make or want speedy recipes for the week that are healthy/comforting and fit your budget. Yes there is a subscription, but you get a 3 day free trial and it’s $10 monthly or $50 annually. Not bad when just trying to find your footing in the kitchen. It caters to the store you shop at, weekly budget, food restrictions and dietary restrictions as well. Even gives you a shopping list with recipe instructions and the nutrition information. Completely recommend.
